changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 2.0.32[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]Usenet with Easynews: faster and lighter[/COLOR]
-Connections open only when playback needs them: it starts with a few, adds more while the video ahead is not arriving fast enough, and closes the extra ones once they are not needed, also while you keep watching or have paused. The setting is now the most it may open: 20 by default (it was 4), up to 60, the most Easynews allows per account. Installs that had 4 move to 20 once.
-Each connection asks for 2 articles at a time, and two playbacks at once never open more than 52 connections, which leaves room for the availability check. If Easynews says "too many connections", playback keeps the ones it has instead of failing.
-New Engine profile: Balanced (the default: 25 s of video read ahead, up to 128 MB of memory) or Efficient (15 s, up to 80 MB). On a device with less than 2 GB of RAM, Balanced works as Efficient by itself, leaving room for the skin and other add-ons.
-The read ahead is worked out from the size and the real length of the film or episode (from 24 MB for an episode to 96 MB for a 4K remux, instead of a fixed 12 MB). The start and the last 8 MB of the file stay in memory, so seeking does not fetch the MKV index again.
-Connections stay alive while paused, so playback resumes at once. Secure connections are set up faster, and the luc_kodi Home rows are not refreshed while a video plays.
-New: two backup Usenet providers, asked in order and only for the pieces Easynews no longer has, at playback and in the availability check. Each one has its server, port, account, connections and a test button.
-Blu-ray M2TS files now play, and RAR releases whose volumes come out of order in the NZB are repaired instead of failing.
-Usenet report: the most connections and memory a playback used, the pieces the backup providers gave, and the date your Easynews plan ends. The log names every slow article.
-Easynews web search leaves out films under 20 minutes and episodes under 5 (extras, trailers and samples).
[COLOR fffdb515]Newznab: up to 3 indexers, careful with your allowance[/COLOR]
-Two more indexers in Settings > Providers > Newznab, each with its Setup Wizard and Test button (altHUB, NinjaCentral, DrunkenSlug, NZBFinder, NZBPlanet, SearchNZB, nzb.life...). All are searched at once, and a release found on two of them is listed once.
-The source list shows which indexer found each result (ALTHUB, NZBGEEK...) where it used to say NEWZNAB, and LOCAL for a Prowlarr or NZBHydra on your home network.
-Newznab results reach the list on the first search: the Easynews availability check waits 1.5 seconds and goes on in the background.
-Each indexer rests when it has used 90% of its daily searches, answers "Too Many Requests" or says its NZB downloads are used up, for an hour or as long as it asks. The availability check leaves the last 3 downloads for playing.
-When the same release is on two indexers and the first gives no NZB, it is taken from the other.
-luc_kodi tells the indexer its own name on every search instead of a random web browser. The log shows each indexer's results and answer time.
-Fixed: a Newznab episode search could fail with "KeyError: 'total_seasons'".
[COLOR fffdb515]When a release does not play[/COLOR]
-If the NZB you pick does not play with Easynews, luc_kodi tries up to 4 more by itself, the ones already found good first, and skips those already found removed. No need to search again.
-If no NZB plays, or 3 in a row were removed from Easynews, it moves on to the next sources that are not Usenet (torrents ready on your debrid), so you still get something to watch.
[COLOR fffdb515]New scrapers: LimeTorrents and BT4G[/COLOR]
-LimeTorrents, on by default, for films, episodes and packs. No other scraper in luc_kodi reached it.
-BT4G, off by default, for films, episodes and packs. It searches the BitTorrent DHT network and finds torrents that are on no torrent site; fake names are filtered by title, year, episode and size. Some internet providers (in Spain, for example) block it, so turn it on in Settings > Providers where it works.
-Both switch to their other address when one does not answer, and a scraper added in an update joins the very first search after updating.
[COLOR fffdb515]Other scrapers and services[/COLOR]
-Torrentio also searches EXT and UIndex.
-TorrentsDB: a "Too Many Requests" answer is no longer retried in the same search; it rests for 20 minutes.
-DMM: since 11 November DMM's free search only serves its own website. luc_kodi now uses DMM's indexer for apps, which needs a DMM API key (Settings > Accounts > Real-Debrid > DMM API key, given to DMM sponsors). DMM is off by default and is switched off once where it was on without a key. The key goes in a request header, never in the log.
-MediaFusion: streams from servers that hide torrent hashes are no longer lost. Premiumize: Account Info opens even without the storage-used field.
-System status: a scraper that brings results is no longer shown in red when its home page is slow.
-Every scraper, debrid, tracking, metadata and AI service was checked against its current public code and documentation.
